newsitem.title: FRANCE: Schneider studies share buyback to up EPS.
newsitem.headline: Schneider studies share buyback to up EPS.

text.p: The chairman of French electrical company Schneider, Didier Pineau-Valencienne, said on Wednesday the company was studying ways of reducing its equity capital in order to boost earnings per share.

"We are studying the possibility of buying back and cancelling a certain number of shares so as to improve earnings per share and avoid the dilution which would come from a convertible bond issue," he told a news conference.
"We'd like to give the market a tangible sign of our will (to improve EPS) through a purchase and cancellation," he said.
The company has 1.7 percent of its shares in treasury stock and does not exclude cancelling those shares, he said, adding the company wanted to find ways of reducing its equity capital.
"We have got almost too much capital," he said.
"We want to show we're looking with the closest attention at the earnings per share...possibly by a reduction of our capital."
He said the company had 137 million shares in circulation and that fully diluted, it would have 150 million shares within two years, other things being equal.
The company has a convertible bond outstanding that is due for conversion and believes the bond holders will take shares since the convertible bond is "in the money".
Schneider shares rose earlier after the company said net attributable profit surged 61.6 percent last year to 1.32 billion francs.
